source: forge-std / foundry testing guidance — own words
title: Proving reentrancy with a reentrant-contract PoC
mechanism: The canonical way to confirm (or refute) a reentrancy finding is a Foundry PoC: a malicious receiver contract that calls back into the target inside the external call, then assert the drain actually occurred.
expected_result: If the target is vulnerable, the recursion drains the target (balance -> 0). If CEI/guarded, the second withdraw reverts and balance stays intact.
confirmation_signals: the callback re-enters a function that reads state mutated AFTER the call
the drain amount exceeds the attacker's legitimately deposited value
the test reproduces >1 withdraw per deposit (recursion) in a single tx
refutation_signals: all state writes precede the call (CEI satisfied) — second withdraw fails its require
a nonReentrant guard is on the re-entered function and reverts
the re-entered path has no shared mutable state with the first call
expected_impact: None for FP refutation; drained funds if confirmed.
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
impact: None for FP refutation; drained funds if confirmed.
remediation: Follow the confirmation/refutation signal checklist before reporting; a refuted PoC is a negative finding, not a vulnerability.

source: foundry fuzz / Echidna guidance — own words
title: Invariant/fuzz testing for accounting (share-value monotonicity)
mechanism: Accounting bugs (rounding, share calc, balance desync) are best verified with an invariant test: define the property that must hold (e.g. user assets never decrease over deposit/withdraw round-trips) and let fuzzing search the state space.
expected_result: Fuzzing finds a counterexample (violation) if the rounding/accounting is exploitable; no violation over the campaign supports a negative finding.
confirmation_signals: a fuzz run produces a counterexample within the campaign (e.g. 10k cases)
the counterexample involves realistic deposit amounts (not only 1-wei edge cases, unless 1-wei is the attack)
pre/post state shows sum(shares) * price != vault assets (ledger desync)
refutation_signals: no counterexample after a long campaign with directed fuzzing of the risky ops
the math is proven by range analysis (all ops bounded and checked)
rounding is provably one-sided in the protocol's favor
test_tooling: foundry forge fuzz / echidna / invariant testing
expected_impact: Loss quantification once a counterexample reproduces.
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
impact: Loss quantification once a counterexample reproduces.
remediation: Follow the confirmation/refutation signal checklist before reporting; a refuted PoC is a negative finding, not a vulnerability.

title: Oracle manipulation PoC with vm.prank/vm.mockCall
mechanism: Oracle findings are verified by mocking the feed/pool state in Foundry: drive the price (prank a large swap, mock latestRoundData with a stale/deviation value) and assert the protocol misprices collateral/borrow.
expected_result: The mocked stale/manipulated price produces a borrow limit or liquidation that is materially wrong (> tolerance) vs the true price.
confirmation_signals: with the mocked price, a user can borrow/withdraw more than the real collateral supports
a stale price changes a liquidation decision (healthy -> liquidatable)
the protocol accepted a price older than its own freshness window
refutation_signals: the protocol's staleness/deviation check reverts the mocked stale price (mock fails -> guard works)
price is TWAP-derived and the single-block mock does not move the window
the mocked price is outside the protocol's accepted deviation band and is rejected
test_tooling: foundry vm.mockCall / vm.prank + vm.warp for TWAP
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
remediation: Follow the confirmation/refutation signal checklist before reporting; a refuted PoC is a negative finding, not a vulnerability.

title: Proving missing access control with a non-privileged caller PoC
mechanism: Access-control findings are verified by calling the privileged function from an unprivileged address in a fork/unit test and asserting it does NOT revert (the vulnerability) or DOES revert (negative finding).
expected_result: The unprivileged caller can execute the privileged effect (mint/upgrade/sweep) — real finding. If it reverts, no finding.
confirmation_signals: the privileged effect executed from a non-owner/non-role address in the test
no modifier/require stood in the way (test proves it)
refutation_signals: the call reverts from unprivileged addresses (modifier present)
the privileged effect requires an additional check not visible in the snippet but present in the path
the caller in the test is actually authorized (test bug)
expected_impact: Full takeover / mint / fund movement if confirmed.
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
impact: Full takeover / mint / fund movement if confirmed.

title: Verifying proxy storage-layout compatibility after upgrade
mechanism: Upgrade findings are verified by deploying the new implementation against the old storage and asserting no slot collision corrupts a value — the standard technique is a slot-layout diff test (forge storage snapshots).
poc_code:
// deploy implV1, set a state var, upgrade to implV2, read the same var
assertEq(proxy.readMyVar(), setValue, 'storage layout mismatch corrupted state');
expected_result: The value survives the upgrade (no collision). If the layout is incompatible, a read returns corrupted data.
confirmation_signals: after upgrade, a previously-set state var reads differently (collision)
the new impl declares a variable at the same slot as a removed one (renamed/deleted)
the upgrade target can selfdestruct or is unverified
refutation_signals: storage snapshot diff is empty (slots identical)
tooling (oz upgrades plugin / forge snapshot) passes the layout check
the new impl only APPENDS new slots
test_tooling: foundry forge + oz-upgrades plugin (storage layout check)
expected_impact: Storage corruption / loss of funds if colliding.
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
impact: Storage corruption / loss of funds if colliding.
remediation: Follow the confirmation/refutation signal checklist before reporting; a refuted PoC is a negative finding, not a vulnerability.

source: foundry deadline/rounding edge test — own words
title: Rounding/precision verification with edge-value fuzzing
mechanism: Rounding findings (division-before-multiplication, floor/ceil direction, dust) are verified by fuzzing edge values — amounts just below 1e18, 1-wei deposits, max-supply — and asserting the deviation from the exact value is bounded and favors the protocol.
expected_result: Each deposit->redeem round-trip loses at most the protocol-favored rounding unit (1 wei or the documented fee). A larger systematic loss is a finding.
confirmation_signals: round-trip loss > 1 wei per op, or accumulates to a material amount over many ops
division-before-multiplication loses more than one unit at a realistic scale
a dust attack cycles small amounts and extracts a material total
refutation_signals: loss is exactly the one-sided rounding unit (favor protocol)
no path lets a third party capture the rounding residual (it accrues to protocol)
preview functions round in the protocol's favor per EIP-4626
root_cause: The vulnerability class this verification pattern proves/refutes; the PoC is the evidence.
preconditions: a candidate finding of this class exists (from static/LLM analysis)
the target contract is deployable in a test harness
remediation: Follow the confirmation/refutation signal checklist before reporting; a refuted PoC is a negative finding, not a vulnerability.
